## Device-side scripts (NOT run by me on the final kit)
Correction to the previous TEST-RESULTS.txt: it said compile_check.py / interp_check.py were "written and
syntax-checked". Neither could run as shipped: compile_check failed on rq (NameError _ASM_UE8M0, blocker 1),
interp_check failed with ModuleNotFoundError 'vllm.models' (blocker 3). Both are fixed now.

- scripts/compile_check.py: the REVIEWER ran it on spark-eight (Triton 3.7.1, cuda:121, 15:18 UTC) on fixA
  (= the tl.constexpr fix only): COMPILE CHECK PASS. The script is unchanged (sha e476088a, same as the reviewer's
  copy) and the kernel source + constants + launch helpers (module lines 1-483) are byte-identical to fixA, so
  that result covers this kit's kernels. Output copied to ref/compile-review-fixA/ (summary.json sha 637b883f...).
- scripts/interp_check.py: the REVIEWER ran it with an equivalent sys.modules harness fix: INTERP CHECK PASS,
  12/12 partial buffers bit-identical (M 1/5/17 x rope, vs, bn128, rope,vs,bn128), 27 s. Log in
  ref/compile-review-fixA/interp.log. The fix is now in the kit's script (registers the base sonar copy as
  vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.ops.sonar_bf16_bmm).
- I could not rerun either on the final kit: ~/dsv41-opt-20261021/CLUSTER_LOCK was held by window w2
  (start 15:21:47Z, eta 19:21:47Z) for the whole fix session, and the brief forbids compiling during a window.
  py_compile only (syntax) on device_test.py, scripts/compile_check.py, scripts/interp_check.py: OK.
  Commands (spark-eight, lock absent):
    mkdir -p ~/climb-scratch/r2-attnout   (copy the kit there)
    cd ~/climb-scratch/r2-attnout && TRITON_CACHE_DIR=$PWD/tcache nice -n 19 ~/venvs/vllm032/bin/python scripts/compile_check.py out
    TRITON_CACHE_DIR=$PWD/tcache nice -n 19 ~/venvs/vllm032/bin/python scripts/interp_check.py
- device_test.py: never run anywhere (the builder has no GPU). HARD GATE for the lead, on a STOPPED node:
    DSV41_ATTNOUT_KIT=<kit dir> ~/venvs/vllm032/bin/python device_test.py --variants all     (exit 0 required)
  No rq-containing arm before 'rq' and 'rope,rq' are bit-identical there. A variant that raises is now
  recorded as failed (exit 1) and the remaining variants still run.
